1.title: Babylon
1.caption: A reconstruction of Babylon and its blue Ishtar Gate, where Daniel was taken as a young man.

1.title: Wisdom from God
1.caption: God gives Daniel understanding in visions and dreams.

3.title: The province of Babylon
3.caption: A reconstruction of Babylon. The image was set up on the plain of Dura in this province.

3.title: Faith under pressure
3.caption: A thematic illustration of standing firm when faith is tested.

4.title: “Is not this great Babylon?”
4.caption: A reconstruction of the city Nebuchadnezzar boasted about in verse 30.

5.title: Given to the Medes and Persians
5.caption: A reconstruction of Persepolis, a Persian royal city. The kingdom passes to Persia that night.

6.title: The kingdom of Darius
6.caption: A reconstruction of a Persian royal city. Daniel now serves the new rulers.

7.title: Daniel’s night vision
7.caption: Daniel writes down what he sees in a dream at night.

7.title: A lion with eagle’s wings
7.caption: The first of four beasts. Verse 17 explains that the beasts are kings, or kingdoms.

7.title: A bear raised up on one side
7.caption: The second beast, with three ribs in its mouth.

7.title: A leopard with four wings and four heads
7.caption: The third beast. Dominion is given to it.

7.title: The fourth beast
7.caption: Dreadful and strong, with great iron teeth and ten horns. A little horn rises among them.

7.title: The court in heaven
7.caption: A thematic illustration of heaven’s sanctuary. Daniel sees thrones set, the Ancient of days seated and the books opened.

8.title: A vision by the river Ulai
8.caption: Daniel’s second vision, two years after the first.

8.title: The ram: Media and Persia
8.caption: Persepolis, a Persian royal city, reconstructed. Gabriel names the ram in verse 20.

8.title: The goat: Grecia
8.caption: Macedonian soldiers, reconstructed. Gabriel names the goat and its first king in verse 21.

8.title: A little horn
8.caption: Horns picture ruling powers. The little horn is not named in this chapter.

8.title: The sanctuary cleansed
8.caption: A thematic illustration of Christ’s ministry in heaven, connected with verse 14 in this study’s interpretation.

8.title: Gabriel explains
8.caption: Gabriel is sent to make Daniel understand the vision.

9.title: Reading Jeremiah
9.caption: Daniel learns from Jeremiah’s book that the exile will last seventy years.

9.title: Gabriel answers the prayer
9.caption: Gabriel arrives while Daniel is still praying.

9.title: Messiah cut off
9.caption: Verse 26 says the Messiah will be cut off, but not for himself. This study connects it with Jesus’ death on the cross.

10.title: By the great river
10.caption: Daniel sees a glorious man clothed in linen.

10.title: Daniel is strengthened
10.caption: A heavenly messenger touches Daniel and gives him strength.

11.title: Persia
11.caption: The vision begins in the days of the Persian kings.

11.title: A mighty king
11.caption: Macedonian soldiers, reconstructed. Most readers see Alexander the Great in verse 3.

11.title: North and south
11.caption: Rival kings struggle for power. The chapter does not name them.

11.title: The time of the end
11.caption: A conceptual illustration of final events.

12.title: A time of trouble
12.caption: A thematic illustration of God’s people holding on to His word in the time of trouble.

12.title: Awake from the dust
12.caption: The empty tomb at dawn, a reminder of the resurrection hope in verse 2.
